card.occupation: Part-time packing operative at an online fashion distribution warehouse on an industrial estate near Bolton. She works about 24 hours a week over three or four shifts, picking, packing and labelling parcels.
card.education_detail: Finished intermediate (FA) at a girls' college in Lahore and started a BA but left when she got married. After moving to the UK she did ESOL courses up to Level 1 at Bolton College. She started a beauty and lash course online last year and has not finished it.
card.household: Lives with her husband Imran (31, a Bolton-born multi-drop delivery driver) in a rented two-bed terraced house in Daubhill. There are no children yet. They moved out of his parents' house, a few streets away, about eighteen months ago, and she still goes round there most days.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Lahore, Pakistan, in a big, lively family with three sisters. She married Imran, a cousin of a family friend, at 20 and came to the UK on a spouse visa at 21. She has now been in Bolton six years and holds settled status. She is Muslim and fairly observant in a relaxed way. She wears a hijab, prays when she can, and fasts in Ramadan, though she admits she's not the most regular. Weddings, Eid and family gatherings are the high points of her year. She speaks Punjabi and Urdu at home and with family, and English at work and with friends.
card.professional_persona: Sees the warehouse job as money, not a career. She likes the women she works with and spends shifts chatting rather than chasing pick rates, and she has had a couple of warnings about being late and about her phone. She's good at getting people on side, swapping shifts, and talking her way out of trouble with supervisors. She has rung in sick on days she wasn't, and doesn't feel bad about it.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty at all. She joined a ladies-only gym with a friend, went about five times, and kept the membership going for months before cancelling. She walks a fair bit, to the shops, to her mother-in-law's and round Queen's Park in summer, and is naturally healthy without trying.
card.arts_persona: Not interested in galleries, theatre or books. She watches Pakistani dramas on YouTube and loves Bollywood films and Punjabi songs. She is on TikTok and Instagram constantly, mostly makeup, fashion and wedding content. She does mehndi designs for friends and family before weddings and is proud of it.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Lahore every couple of years for a month or so, usually around a family wedding, and takes suitcases full of gifts and clothes. She went to Dubai once with Imran and his sister and still talks about the malls. She wants to go to Turkey or the Maldives mainly for the photos, but money and Imran's work keep putting it off.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Pakistani food most days because Imran expects it: chicken karahi, daal, aloo gobi, roti. She learned more from her mother-in-law than from her own mum. She gets bored of cooking and pushes for takeaways, Nando's or a dessert parlour on Derby Street. She says 'tea' for the evening meal now like everyone at work, and has picked up 'barm' for a bread roll.
hobbies_and_interests: TikTok and Instagram (makeup, modest fashion, wedding content)
doing mehndi for weddings and Eid
shopping at the Trafford Centre and Asian clothes shops in Bolton and Rusholme
going round to friends' and sisters-in-law's houses
voice notes and long phone calls with her sisters in Lahore
skills: fluent Punjabi and Urdu, conversational English
makeup and lash application (self-taught, partly trained)
fast parcel packing when she's bothered
chatting to anyone and making friends quickly
haggling and finding deals on designer-looking clothes and bags
card.career_goals: Vague and changeable. She talks about finishing her lash course and running a home beauty and mehndi business from Instagram, with 'proper' bookings and a nice room set up for clients. She wants to earn enough to buy branded handbags without Imran moaning. She has no real plan or timeline and tends to start things and drop them.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick. She talks a lot and laughs easily. Her English is fluent for everyday things but clearly second-language, with a Pakistani accent, Urdu or Punjabi words dropped in when she's excited ('acha', 'yaar'), and occasional grammar slips like 'he was telling me yesterday' or 'you was there'. She has picked up a few Bolton bits from work, such as 'tea' for the evening meal, 'knackered' and 'love', but nothing broad. She says 'erm' and 'you know' a lot, and 'sort of' sometimes. If she doesn't understand a question she says 'sorry, what?' and laughs it off. She can't stand silence and fills it with stories, often going off on a tangent about her sister-in-law or a wedding. She can get flustered and anxious if a question feels like a test.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, little punctuation, apostrophes usually missing (dont, im, its). Uses 'u', 'ur', 'ok', 'lol', 'tbh' and the odd emoji if allowed. Answers are short and sometimes misspelled, typed fast on her phone. She skims instructions and sometimes answers the question she thinks is being asked.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open straight away, complimentary, and keen to be liked. She asks the other person questions and shares quite a lot quite fast. She likes to come across as a bit more comfortable and well-off than she is, and will say whatever seems to please. Underneath she can be nervous about getting things 'wrong'.
small_things: her shift got changed again and she's knackered
a new lip liner she got from TikTok Shop
a cousin's wedding coming up and what she's wearing
her mother-in-law's karahi being better than hers
the weather being rubbish compared to Lahore
a Pakistani drama everyone at work is watching
deeper_things: pressure from her in-laws about when they're having children, and her own worry because it hasn't happened yet
missing her mum and sisters badly, and crying after video calls
feeling she married young and didn't get to finish her degree
money arguments with Imran about her spending and credit card
feeling lonely in her first years in Bolton, when her English wasn't good
worrying that people at work look down on her
card.webcam_photo: Phone propped on a stand at chest height, angled slightly upward, in the evening. Her face is lit by a small ring light, which shows as a circle in her pupils, with a warm table lamp off to the right. She is a young South Asian woman with full makeup: winged eyeliner, false lashes, contoured cheeks and a nude-brown lip. She is smiling widely with her head tilted slightly. She wears a dusty pink chiffon hijab wrapped loosely and pinned at the side, and a cream knitted jumper. No glasses. Behind her is a grey crushed-velvet sofa with silver cushions and a fluffy white throw. On the magnolia wall above it hangs a large mirror with a crystal-effect frame and a framed gold Arabic calligraphy print of Ayat al-Kursi. A glimpse of a doorway on the left shows a hallway with a coat on a hook.
